solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Back new skills to turn around SPFL club (9)

indicators.note: something turned around faces the other way, so the whole string is read backwards

annotation.surface: A fan urges a struggling Scottish football club to back its young talent and turn the season around.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole chain REAR-N-ARTS is turned round in one go. The SPFL is the Scottish Professional Football League, and Stranraer is a small club on the Galloway coast.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Stranraer FC is one of the member clubs of the Scottish Professional Football League.

entries.clue: Theatre employee departs after agent has changed (5,4)

indicators.note: letters that have changed no longer sit in their first order, so AGENT HAS is rearranged
after means following, so D is placed behind the rearranged letters

blocks.note: d. = departs, as on a timetable

annotation.surface: A theatre worker quits once their agent has been replaced.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Departs' looks like the verb of the story, but it only supplies the timetable abbreviation D.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain job title: stagehands are the backstage crew a theatre employs to shift scenery and props.

entries.clue: Person getting up from chair is erudite (5)

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the answer is lifted straight out of the words that follow

annotation.surface: Someone rising from their seat turns out to be learned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Person getting up from chair' reads as one long definition, but the definition stops at 'up' and 'from' starts the hunt.
annotation.definitionFit: A riser is one who rises, the sense in 'an early riser' for someone who gets up at dawn.

entries.clue: Retiring janitor shows ID attached to uniform? (4,3)

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the word goes backwards

blocks.note: a gateman keeps a gate, like a janitor or doorkeeper

annotation.surface: A caretaker about to retire shows his ID badge pinned to his uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like a janitor leaving his job; here it means going backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: a badge pinned to a uniform is one place a tag identifying the wearer is found.

entries.clue: Element against removing European from capital (8)

indicators.note: removing means taking away, so E is taken out of the word for capital

annotation.surface: Sounds like a political stance: being against removing Europeans from a capital city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city, but it is money in the financial sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: antimony, symbol Sb, is one of the chemical elements, a brittle silvery metalloid.

entries.clue: Snub oddly rejected 'green expert' (6)

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions are rejected, thrown out, keeping only the even ones

blocks.note: a buff is an expert enthusiast, as in 'film buff'

annotation.surface: Someone brushes off a so-called environmental expert, strangely turning them down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' seems to describe the snub, but it tells you to drop the odd letters of 'green'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as verbs: to snub an approach and to rebuff it both mean to reject it curtly.

entries.clue: Initial temperature becoming cold for which songbird? (4)

indicators.note: becoming means turning into, so the initial T turns into C

blocks.note: first letter T (temperature) swapped for C (cold)

annotation.surface: A quizzical question about which bird the first chill of the season turns up.
annotation.walkthrough: The swap works on the word hidden behind 'which', so the clue reads backwards: find THAT first, then change its first T.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the chats, such as the stonechat and whinchat, are small songbirds.

entries.clue: Weight vanishes surprisingly when taking drug (9)

indicators.note: letters arranged surprisingly land in an unexpected order, so VANISHES is rearranged
taking means taking in, so the fodder absorbs E

annotation.surface: A dieter's weight drops unexpectedly once they start on some medication.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a weight-loss story, yet the answer is weight itself, not its loss.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the heaviness of a thing is how much it weighs.

entries.clue: Book inscription (5)

blocks.note: publishers count their list of books one by one
a heading written on a page or cover

annotation.walkthrough: 'Book inscription' reads as one thing, a signed dedication, but it is two separate meanings.
annotation.definitionFit: Publishers call each book on their list a title, and a title is also the inscription or heading on a page.

entries.clue: Creature using paws to grab lemur's tail, right? (6)

indicators.note: paws that grab something hold it inside them, so FEET enclose the other letters
the tail of a word is its end, so lemur gives its last letter

annotation.surface: An animal grabbing a lemur by the tail with its paws, checking it has it right.
annotation.walkthrough: Both Rs sit inside the paws: FE-RR-ET.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a ferret is a creature, a domesticated animal of the weasel family.

entries.clue: Tea dunderhead gets early in the day (5)

annotation.surface: A fool gets up early for his morning tea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tea' looks like part of the fool's morning routine, but it is the definition standing at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Assam is a strong black tea named after the Indian state where it grows.

entries.clue: Suggests key condiment that's fine (5,4)

blocks.note: to table a motion is to put it forward
the Alt key on a computer keyboard

annotation.surface: Someone recommends a seasoning that is perfectly fine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine' is not approval but texture: table salt is finely ground. 'Key' suggests a musical note but is a keyboard key.
annotation.definitionFit: Table salt is the finely ground salt put out as a condiment, so 'fine' describes its grain rather than its quality.

entries.clue: Mistake in writing amount Laura rued occasionally on reflection (7)

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken
a reflection in a mirror shows things backwards

annotation.surface: Laura regrets writing down the wrong amount, now she thinks about it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' reads as Laura thinking it over; in the wordplay it is a mirror image.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from Latin: an erratum is an error in writing or print, listed on an errata slip.

entries.clue: Over time hide this writer's secret (7)

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece over another comes first, so FUR goes before T

annotation.surface: A writer confides that over time they have hidden a secret.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: an animal's skin.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adjectives: a furtive glance is a secret, sly one.

entries.clue: Conceited mimic, initially ignored, Harry flipping plugs (8)

indicators.note: the initial letter is ignored, so the P of PARROT is left out
flipping over turns a word end to end, so NAG becomes GAN
a plug fills a hole, so GAN goes into the middle of ARROT

annotation.surface: A vain impersonator, snubbed at first, is exasperated by a man called Harry who keeps flip-flopping.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the verb to harry, to nag.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: conceited and arrogant both describe someone with too high an opinion of themselves.

entries.clue: Answer from Germany stopping one seeking to overturn Brexit? (9)

indicators.note: a stopper sits in a gap, so D stops up the middle of REJOINER

blocks.note: someone who wants the UK to rejoin the EU
D = Deutschland, the international vehicle code for Germany

annotation.surface: A German reply that blocks a campaigner trying to reverse Brexit.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags REJOINER as an invented word, earned by the Brexit context.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rejoinder is an answer, usually a quick or sharp one.

entries.clue: Scottish banker with cute daughter (5)

annotation.surface: An Edinburgh banker and his sweet little daughter.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is often a river, which has banks; the Tweed runs along the Scottish border.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: a banker is something with banks, a river, and the Tweed is a Scottish one.

entries.clue: He's due regularly to test out something decorators use? (9)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter of TO TEST is taken
letters that are out are out of place, so they are rearranged

annotation.surface: A man is scheduled to try out some kit that decorators use.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Test out' reads as trying something, but 'test' is fodder and 'out' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: decorators spread dust sheets over furniture and floors while painting.

entries.clue: Keep in check boldness on horseback (6,2)

blocks.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

annotation.surface: A rider needs nerve to keep a horse under control.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for courage. A jockey riding a horse is said to be 'up', as in 'Dettori up'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to bottle up feelings is to keep them in check, sealed away as if in a bottle.

entries.clue: Jack visits Céline in French city (5)

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside the host's home, so J goes inside DION

blocks.note: J = jack in a pack of cards

annotation.surface: A man called Jack calls on the singer Céline at her home in France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Céline' stands for her surname, not her first name.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Dijon, famous for its mustard, is a city in Burgundy in eastern France.

entries.clue: Legal official, indiscreet after downing whiskey (6)

indicators.note: a drink that has been downed is gone, so W disappears from NOT WARY

blocks.note: W in the NATO alphabet, removed

annotation.surface: A lawyer gets loose-lipped after knocking back a whisky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Downing' suggests drinking, but it means taking the W out.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a notary is a legal official authorised to witness and certify documents.

entries.clue: Giant firm, American, must conceal deficit (8)

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so CO and US hide LOSS between them

annotation.surface: A huge American corporation has to hide its shortfall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Giant' sits beside 'firm' as if describing a giant company, but it is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, after the Colossus of Rhodes, a giant statue: anything colossal-sized is a colossus.

entries.clue: Periodically boy led round of applause for veteran (3,4)

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

annotation.surface: A youngster leads the clapping for an old soldier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Veteran' paints an old soldier, but here it means someone long experienced.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: an old hand is a veteran in the sense of someone with long experience at a job.

entries.clue: Villains identify fences doing time (6)

indicators.note: a fence encloses, so the outer words fence in the answer

annotation.surface: Criminals point out the receivers of stolen goods who are serving sentences.
annotation.walkthrough: A fence is a receiver of stolen goods, which makes the crime story convincing, but here it means enclose.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang: a prisoner is said to be inside, the same state as doing time.

entries.clue: Composer of national broadcast (7)

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, not seen, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a Briton is a British national

annotation.surface: A composer featured in a national radio broadcast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'National broadcast' suggests the BBC; 'national' is a noun meaning a citizen.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Benjamin Britten, who wrote Peter Grimes, is among the best-known English composers.

entries.clue: Show embarrassment when US president pens drivel ultimately (5)

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in, as sheep in a pen, so BUSH encloses L
ultimately means in the end, so drivel gives its last letter

annotation.surface: A president should be embarrassed when he writes nonsense.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pens' looks like writing, but it means enclosing.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb for the outward sign: reddening in the face is how you show embarrassment.

entries.clue: Name for cat, typically small, written by Potter (7)

indicators.note: written by means set down beside, so S follows TIDDLE

blocks.note: to tiddle is to potter or trifle

annotation.surface: A cat's name that sounds like something Beatrix Potter might have written.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like Beatrix Potter, author of animal tales, but it is the verb to potter.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional stock name: Tiddles is the typical British name for a pet cat, like Rover for a dog.

entries.clue: Mood essentially within London university is relaxed (5)

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so mood gives its middle letters
within means inside, so OO goes inside LSE

annotation.surface: The atmosphere at a London college is basically laid-back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mood' suggests the atmosphere of the place, but only its middle two letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: loose limbs or a loose grip are relaxed, not tight.

entries.clue: Destroy two foreign articles belonging to me (9)

annotation.surface: Someone orders two imported items of theirs to be destroyed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Articles' looks like objects, but it means the grammatical words 'a' and 'the'.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: to undermine is to wreck something gradually, as by digging beneath its foundations.

entries.clue: In agreement when lunch could be served? (2,3)

blocks.note: united in view, of one mind
a typical lunchtime on the clock

annotation.surface: Two people agree over what time lunch might be served.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful definition, hence the question mark: one o'clock is a usual lunchtime.
annotation.definitionFit: To be at one with someone is to agree with them, and lunch is often served at one o'clock.

entries.clue: That girl's love for leading man (4)

annotation.surface: A girl is in love with the star of the film.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Love' looks like the girl's feelings, but it is the tennis score, nil.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from stage and screen: the leading man of a story is its hero.

entries.clue: Index Pete adjusted as appropriate (9)

indicators.note: letters that are adjusted are moved about, so INDEX PETE is rearranged

annotation.surface: Pete tweaked the index as he saw fit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As appropriate' reads as one phrase, but 'as' is only the link and 'appropriate' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adjectives: an expedient course is one that is appropriate or convenient for the purpose.
